answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a continuity bond: every identity locks collateral that only vests after a long horizon of useful work — like timber seasoning on a terrace before it can bear weight. A single attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand bonds and wait the full horizon for each, so the cost of faking scale dwarfs any short-term reward. If two identities ever show identical behavior fingerprints, both bonds are slashed, turning duplication itself into the evidence that pays for its own punishment.
